doc.title: Bob Stewart interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

title: Jazz education, Jazz at Lincoln Center and Ken Burns
summary: He weighs the pros and cons of jazz schools, second-hand knowledge, and Lincoln Center and the Ken Burns series.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: What do you think jazz education has done for the music as far as — we’ve got lots of places to go now to study and to be a jazz musician. Has it changed the way the music is developing do you think?
I’m sure it has. It’s kind of like what we spoke about earlier, an integration, and Jackie Robinson getting into the pro leagues.

It has its pros and cons. I mean he got into the pro leagues but it meant the death of the Negro League. There are a lot of schools that have jazz programs and they graduate these students who have never really played with anybody and so therefore a lot of their information has come from somebody who has never played with anybody.

Exactly. So they’re getting second hand information and then the school hires them to teach. And so now they’re giving third hand information, none of which they know first hand. And that’s, I mean it’s great that jazz is being taught, you know what I mean? People will ask me the question well what do you think about what Wynton’s doing down at Jazz at Lincoln Center. What do you think about what he’s doing? Or they’ll ask me about the Ken Burns Jazz, say what do you think about that. And I’ll say well you
know it’s better than the last one they put out. And they’ll say well which was the last one they put out? I’ll say there wasn’t none.
Would you rather that they didn’t do it?
Or that there wasn’t a Jazz at Lincoln Center?
Exactly. I say there wasn’t none. I say that’s the one it’s better than.
Yeah. I have to remember that.

Okay. And they’ll say well what was the other one, I’m trying to remember, what was the other one? And I’ll say it wasn’t none. So it’s definitely better than what was going on before. It has to start somewhere.
